Name: Gallio
Summary: Gallio was the proconsul of Achaia before whom the Jews brought Paul at Corinth, accusing him of persuading men to worship contrary to the law. Gallio dismissed the case as a matter of words and names, and cared for none of the beating that followed.
KeyStory: Gallio refused to judge Paul's doctrine, calling it a question of words and names, and the case collapsed.
LifeLesson: Gallio's indifference freed Paul and left Sosthenes beaten. A judge who cares for nothing protects no one.
